title: Moderate head injury after a motorcycle crash, 35-year-old man
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Motorcycle accident 1 hour ago; hit his head, vomited twice and is confused.
intake.trauma_mechanism: Motorcyclist versus car at about 50 km/h, helmet on

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: Level 2 comes from two cells. TRAUMA, HEAD NECK Level 2 column (p11, x~131): 'Altered Mental State' (confused), plus 'High velocity' if 50 km/h counts. Primary triage Conscious Levels Level 2 column (p4, x~246): 'Confused, agitated, disoriented'. The Vital Signs L2 cell 'GCS < 13 or drop > 2' (p7) is NOT met: GCS is 13, and a drop from an assumed 15 is only 2. Pain 6 is Level 3. No Level 1 cell applies (airway intact, no shock). The QR Head Injury triage algorithm would give Yellow zone (step 3, motorcycle crash > 30 km/h); MTS is used here. B: Level 2 comes from the TRAUMA, HEAD NECK complaint cells 'Altered Mental State' and 'High velocity' (x~131, p11), and from the Rapid Assessment cell 'Confused, agitated, disoriented' (x~246, p4). GCS 13 does NOT meet the vital-signs cell 'GCS < 13 or drop > 2' (x~131, p7), but a GCS drop of more than 2 on re-triage would. Pain 6 is a Level 3 cell. No Level 1 cell applies (airway intact, not in shock, not unresponsive).

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Severity label: the case title says 'moderate', but KKM CPG/QR classify GCS 13 as mild head injury (MHI 13-15; moderate is 9-12). Both labels are accepted.

Triage: 50 km/h motorcyclist vs car. Whether this counts as MTS 'High velocity' (L2) is a judgement call; 'Altered Mental State' gives L2 regardless. The QR head-injury triage algorithm would give Yellow zone.

drugs_forbidden is left empty. The head-injury CPG has no explicit 'avoid' statement that applies to this GCS-13, normotensive patient. Albumin harm is shown only in severe TBI; the 'diuretics should not be used' warning is for hypotensive patients.
Whether 'GCS <15 at 2 hours after injury' will be met cannot be known at triage (injury was 1 h ago). Vomiting >= 2 already qualifies him for immediate CT.
B: The case title says 'moderate head injury', but the MOH CPG classes GCS 13 as mild head injury (GCS 13-15, at the high-risk end). The diagnosis match accepts both; the adjudicator should decide whether a report calling it 'mild' or 'moderate' is penalised.

There are no drugs_forbidden. The CPG warns only that diuretics should not be used in hypotensive patients (he is not hypotensive) and reports worse outcomes with albumin in severe TBI, without an explicit 'avoid' for this patient.
